claims.claim: Cognex industrial machine vision sits directly in the factory/warehouse automation loop: sensing and edge inference support inspection, identification and quality/throughput decisions, connecting AI vision technology to manufacturing and distribution efficiency needs.

The structural opportunity is broad but not monopolistic: Cognex itself identifies competing machine-vision vendors, component/controller suppliers, system integrators, customer internal engineering and open-source AI tools as substitutes, so resilience depends on deployment simplicity, performance and integration rather than irreplaceability.

Cognex's 2026 product expansion toward embedded AI and real-time inference can reduce the skill/latency bottleneck for deploying vision at production-line speed; the successor bottleneck becomes customer-scale integration, measurable economics and durable adoption across sites.

causalEdges.mechanism: edge sensing and inference convert visual production data into real-time decisions
faster defect detection, traceability and process decisions can reduce manual inspection and quality losses
lower specialist burden and line-compatible inference can broaden feasible applications

risks.risk: Competing vision vendors, internal engineering and open-source AI make the technology layer substitutable; durable value capture requires product/integration advantages that remain observable in customer adoption and economics.
Four large end markets represented about 85% of 2025 revenue, creating scenario sensitivity to industrial and electronics/logistics capital cycles even with a broad customer base.

unknowns.unknown: Current evidence does not quantify switching costs, OneVision attach/renewal economics, or the share of customer workflows where Cognex has uniquely defensible control rather than replaceable component status.

claims.claim: The strongest present challenge to a high-confidence moat thesis is substitution rather than evidence of accounting distress: Cognex discloses competition from machine-vision vendors, component suppliers, system integrators, customer engineering teams and open-source AI tools.

Revenue exposure is diversified by customer count but concentrated by end market: logistics, packaging, consumer electronics and automotive together were about 85% of 2025 revenue, leaving cyclical/concentration sensitivity that can pressure adoption and pricing simultaneously.

Recent issuer adoption claims are directionally useful but do not by themselves prove durable share gains, pricing power or production-scale economics; those claims should be tested against subsequent financial and customer evidence rather than treated as a blocker today.

causalEdges.mechanism: credible alternatives constrain lock-in and can shift value toward integrators/customers
capex slowdowns across dominant verticals can synchronize demand weakness

risks.risk: Confidence inflation risk if early OneVision customer counts or product performance claims are extrapolated into durable economic moat without attach-rate, renewal, margin or share evidence.
End-market concentration can amplify industrial-capex cyclicality despite more than 30,000 customers globally.

unknowns.unknown: No current packet evidence establishes material dilution/financing stress, customer-level concentration, or a present governance defect; absence of such evidence is retained as uncertainty rather than a fabricated negative finding.
